units.title: Five ways to keep your camp cosy this winter!
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Hello, adventurer! The nights are drawing in, so here are our five favourite ways to keep camp cosy: 1. Layer up with a merino base. 2. Keep a kettle on the go. 3. Hang a lantern by the door (ours are the brightest in the Sound!). 4. Insulate under your bedding, not just over it. 5. Good company! This week only, 15% off fleece blankets in store and online. Stay warm out there! The Camp Supply team

units.title: Week two: a few things
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi,
Hope the drizzle isn't too bad out there. A few things for the week:
- Daily tally sheets please by 19:00 so payroll can match them.
- Fuel mix: head office has switched supplier, the new cans are green not red, same ratio.
- The client remains very hands-off and is happy for us to get on with it.
- Just checking where we are on numbers when you have a moment, no rush.
Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Sorry, one more. The manufacturer has recalled a batch of chainsaw trousers with a faulty protective layer. Labels with a lot number ending in 47 or 48 are affected. If any of the crew have those, please take them out of use and let me know sizes, and I'll get replacements on the next boat.
Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Crew pay
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi,
Payroll have flagged that the crew's day rates are behind on the site account. I'm sure you're on top of it, but could you let me know when you expect to clear it? I'd much rather sort it before the end of the week than have it come up on the Monday call with head office. People notice when pay is late, out there especially.
Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Leaver paperwork
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi,
I've seen the note that one of the crew has left the site. Sorry to hear it, these things happen on long jobs. Could you:
- confirm their last working day,
- make sure any company kit is signed back in,
- let me know if you want me to look for a replacement, though I can't promise anyone quickly at this time of year.
Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Post and paperwork via Gilliver
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi,
The ferries have been running late in the drizzle, so I've asked the courier to leave anything addressed to the site at the Gilliver harbour office rather than trying to meet the boat. The harbourmaster has kindly agreed to hold it. Nothing urgent coming, just the signed insurance schedule and the new risk assessment forms.
Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Saw servicing reminder
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi,
A reminder that company policy is a chain and bar check every day and a fuller service every 40 running hours. On a job like this that comes round fast. If you're short of spare chain or files, tell me and I'll add them to the next order on our side. Prices are up again, so I'd rather order once and order properly.
Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Just checking in on numbers
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi,
Just checking where we are on numbers. Head office are asking whether we'll reach a quarter of the island by the end of the week, and I said I'd ask you rather than guess. I know the first days on a big site are always slower while the camp settles in. If there's anything that would speed things up, people or kit, please say.
Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Quarter mark
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi,
The tallies show you're past a quarter of the island, which head office were very pleased to see. Well done to you and the crew. I'll pass it on to the client in Monday's call, though I expect they'll just say 'thank you' as usual. Keep an eye on everyone's hands and backs; the second quarter is where people get tired.
Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Why did the tree go to the dentist?
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text:
To get a root canal. You're welcome, chief.
Road job's going fine, if fine means rain and a JCB with a personality disorder. We're two days behind because the council keeps finding badgers. How's island life? Is it all sea views and chainsaws? Don't let Ruth work you to the bone. She'll ask nicely, which is worse.
Hal

units.author: hal_brannock
units.text:
PS forgot to say, my lad passed his chainsaw ticket. Nineteen and already better at sharpening than me. I've told him there's no money in trees and he's ignored me, which is the first sign of a proper feller. If you ever need a keen one who talks too much, he's yours.
Hal

units.title: rehearsal news!!
units.author: sam
units.text: hi you, big news from the school, Pip got the part of the lighthouse keeper in the play, which has nine lines and a lantern, and she's been practising them on Moss, who now looks alarmed whenever anyone says 'the light must never go out'. the costume is your old raincoat, I hope you don't mind, it's been in the loft for years. anyway I'll send you the date when they decide. love, S x

units.title: rehearsal news (sort of)
units.author: sam
units.text: hi you, news from the school, Pip didn't get the lighthouse keeper part, she's been cast as 'the fog', which means a grey sheet and a lot of slow walking across the stage. she was crushed for a whole hour and is now taking it very seriously and drifts down the hall at home to practise. Moss follows her and barks. anyway I'll send the date when there is one. love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: also forgot to say, Moss has been forgiven for the glove, mostly. we found the other half of it in her basket today, which she defended with her life. the vet says she's fine and that labradors 'just do that'. Mum came round and said she'd have had her hide, then fed her half a biscuit. that's Mum. love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: I tried to attach a photo of Pip rehearsing and it says the file's too big, so you'll have to imagine her standing on the kitchen chair holding a torch with enormous seriousness. I'll try again tomorrow from the library computer, it's better than my phone. sleep well out there, if you can with all the sawing. S x

units.title: Sorry to write again
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hello, I'm sorry to write to you again. Tomas's phone isn't getting my messages, I think, or he can't reply from there. Could you tell him I'm fine and that the boiler man came and fixed it? He was worried about that before he left. And, if you don't mind me asking, is he sleeping? He never sleeps well in a new place. Thank you, and sorry. Ana

units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: PS I'm sorry, I meant to say thank you for letting the crew have the evenings to themselves. Tomas said in his last message that the fire is nice and that the boss doesn't shout. I know that's not much, but from him it is a lot. Ana

units.title: FW: Harbour notice on slipways
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi,
Forwarding this from the Gilliver harbourmaster, for information. The slipways at Gilliver and Lisle are now closed to pedestrians from sunset to sunrise under a harbour byelaw, and a chain goes across the Gilliver slip at night. It doesn't affect scheduled boats, but please remind the crew not to wait on the slip after dark if they're ever on the mainland.
Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
To add: the harbourmaster says the key to the chain is held at the harbour office and at the chandlery, so a late landing is fine as long as someone rings ahead. I've put both numbers on the contact sheet. I gather there's been some talk locally about people on the slips at night. I'm sure it's anglers.
Thanks, Ruth

units.title: First aid kit: restock list
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi,
The insurer has asked us to confirm the site first-aid kit is complete. Could you check for:
- large wound dressings (at least four),
- the burns gel,
- the foil blankets,
- eye wash,
- the trauma tourniquet, still sealed.
If anything has been used, let me know and I'll replace it. No paperwork needed beyond a yes.
Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Weekly risk assessment sign-off
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi,
The weekly risk assessment is due for sign-off. The new forms are waiting at the Gilliver harbour office; until they reach you, a note in the site log is fine. The usual headings: felling near the shore, fuel storage, fire, weather, fatigue. Please don't skip fatigue, the insurer reads that one.
Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Sorry, I should have said: under weather, please note the deep low forecast for the end of the week. If it comes in as the Met Office expect, there may be a day with no felling at all. That's fine. A lost day is better than a tree on the camper. I'll explain it to head office.
Thanks, Ruth

units.title: From head office
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi,
Mr Grieve asked me to pass on his thanks for keeping things running out there. He doesn't send many of those, so take it while it's going. He also asked whether you have everything you need, and I said I'd ask. It's an ordinary clearance, just a big one, and he knows that big ones are hard on everyone.
Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Client call moved
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi,
The weekly client call has moved from Monday morning to Monday afternoon at the client's request. You don't need to be on it; I'll report from the tallies. If there's anything you'd like me to raise with them, about access, the landing stage or anything else, let me know by Sunday evening.
Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi,
Following up on yesterday's note about crew pay, as payroll are still showing a balance on the site account. I don't want to nag. But the crew can see their statements, and in my experience nothing makes a long job feel longer than being owed. If it's a cash-flow problem on your side, please tell me and we'll find a way.
Thanks, Ruth

units.author: hal_brannock
units.text:
Another one: what's a tree's favourite drink? Root beer. I'll stop when you beg.
Pay came in this morning, two days late, which for Grieve is practically early. They pay late but they pay, chief. Ruth sends my statements with a little 'sorry for the delay' line and I believe she means it. She's decent, for management.
Hal

units.title: serious for a second
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text:
Serious for a second. Keep a good fire going at night, and keep the crew round it. Not for warmth, for heads. Long jobs in the middle of nowhere get into people. You'll know if one of them's going quiet, so don't wait for them to say it.
Anyway. The JCB has a name now, it's Gerald, and Gerald has eaten a fence.
Hal

units.title: Mum's letter came
units.author: sam
units.text: hi, Mum's hospital letter came this morning, the hip operation is booked for next week, with a pre-op check on Monday. she's pretending she's not nervous by reorganising her kitchen cupboards. I'll take her to both. you're not to worry, she says she'd rather you finished your job than sat in a waiting room with her reading old magazines. love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: she also asked me to tell you 'to wear a proper hat'. I said you were a grown adult who has worn a hat all your life. she said 'tell them anyway'. so: wear a proper hat. that's from Mum, not me. I personally don't care about your hat. S x

units.author: sam
units.text: anyway, Sound FM had a thing on this afternoon about someone standing on a slipway at night and the harbourmaster putting a chain across it. Mum says it'll be a fisherman who didn't want to pay for a licence. I thought of you, because it's that bit of coast, isn't it? I hope the boats are behaving. S x

units.author: sam
units.text: tried the photo from the library computer and the library computer said no too, so it's officially cursed. the library's doing a local history display this month, lots of old photos of the Sound, the herring girls, the lighthouse when it had keepers. I'll take a picture of it for you if the camera ever forgives me. S x

units.title: Just one thing
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hello, I'm sorry, just one small thing. Tomas's birthday is next week. I've sent a card to the Grieve office in Port Ammet, as Ruth said post goes from there. If it reaches you, please could you give it to him? You don't have to say anything. He'll know it's from me. Thank you. Ana

units.author: hal_brannock
units.text:
PS: I was on a Grieve crew years back with a few lads who'd done islands before. Good fellers, all of them. Funny lot about the evenings, though, they'd always want the lamps lit early. Anyway, I'm sure yours are fine. Gerald sends his regards, and an apology to the fence.
Hal

units.title: Storm on the way? Be ready with our top picks!
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Wild weather ahead! Make sure you're storm-ready with our top picks: heavy-duty tarp clips, ground pegs that actually stay in, a wind-up radio, and of course our famous lanterns, the brightest in the Sound. Plus: free guy-rope tensioners with every tent order this weekend. Batten down, brew up, and enjoy the drama from somewhere dry! The Camp Supply team

units.title: Weekend weather
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi,
The Met Office now have a gale coming through late on day 13 and into day 14. Before it arrives, please:
- lash down tarps and anything loose around the camper,
- don't fell anything leaning toward the camp once the wind gets up,
- fill the water and fuel cans,
- keep the crew close to camp on the worst night.
Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Also, the ferry and supply boats may not run on the worst day, so any order that would normally arrive then could slip by a day. I'll chase on our side. If anything at the camp gets damaged, photographs for the insurer please, but only once it's safe to take them.
Thanks, Ruth

units.title: A note about online chatter
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi,
You may have seen some talk about the Holm on local forums and in the Courier's letters page, mostly guesses about what the client wants it for. Nothing to worry about, and nothing for us to respond to. I'd just ask that nobody on the crew posts about the site, the client or the work. If anyone contacts you asking questions, please send them to me.
Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
I should say, that isn't because there's anything to hide. It's an ordinary clearance, just a big one, and the client simply prefers to keep themselves to themselves. Grieve always asks crews not to discuss a client's site in public. I'd have sent the same note on any job.
Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Insurance schedule
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi,
The signed insurance schedule for the site is now at the Gilliver harbour office with the other post. It needs to be kept on site with the first-aid kit, ideally in the camper. The insurer may ask for a photo of it pinned up. I know it's paperwork, but it's the kind that matters if anything goes wrong.
Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi,
Following up on the leaver. Payroll have processed their final pay. Head office asked me whether there was any problem on site that I should know about. I said no, people leave long jobs for all sorts of reasons. If there was anything, though, I'd rather hear it from you than from anyone else.
Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Numbers before the weekend
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi,
Just checking we'll have tallies in for days 12 and 13 before the weather arrives, so the Monday report isn't missing two days. I'll report the gale day as weather, not as lost time. Head office are fine with that. They're less fine with gaps, so a short note is better than no sheet.
Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
And thank you, by the way, for keeping the sheets tidy. I've had site leads on other jobs send me tallies on the back of a fuel receipt. You know who you are, as they say. (Not you.)
Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Weather report from a professional
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text:
What did the big tree say to the little tree in the gale? Leaf me alone. That one was weak, I'll admit it.
Saw the forecast. If it's anything like the one we had on the Lisle verge job, tie everything down twice and sleep in your boots. Don't fell in the wind, chief, I don't care what Ruth's spreadsheet says.
Hal

units.author: hal_brannock
units.text:
Mind you, Ruth will tell you the same. She's sound about weather. It's deadlines she gets twitchy about, and only because head office leans on her. Give her a nice tidy tally before the storm and she'll defend you to the end of the earth.
Gerald has been repaired and is sulking.
Hal

units.author: hal_brannock
units.text:
PS ignore what I said yesterday about lamps, that was just old crew talk, I'd had a long day. Get some sleep. When the job's done we'll have a pint and you can tell me how many trees and I'll pretend I've done more.
Hal

units.title: storm coming!
units.author: sam
units.text: hi, the radio keeps saying gales for the weekend, so I've tied the bins to the fence and taken the washing line down and Moss has decided the whole thing is a game. are you all right out there for wind? I know you'll say yes. Pip asked if your tent will blow away and I said you live in a proper camper with a door. anyway please be careful. love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: the Evening Post had a bit about that tower block in Weyhaven where the stairwell lights keep going off, the landlord says it's a relay, the tenants say it's been weeks. Mum read it out and said 'that's what you get for building them so high'. I think it's what you get for landlords. anyway that's my politics for the night. S x

units.author: sam
units.text: ok last one, I promise. Pip's teacher asked if anyone had a relative who 'works outdoors in an interesting place' for a show-and-tell, and Pip put her hand up and said you were 'cutting down a whole island'. the class were very impressed. I said I'd ask whether you'd write her a few lines about it when you're back. no pressure. S x

units.title: The storm
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hello, I'm sorry, I saw the forecast and I wanted to ask you to tell Tomas I'm fine and I have candles and the torch he left me. He'll worry about me before he worries about himself. My friend in Dellow Court says their landlord blamed a relay for the stairs, so that's something sorted at least. Thank you for reading these. Ana

units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: I'm sorry, one more thing. I heard from someone at the Grieve office that one of the crew has left. Please could you tell me if Tomas is all right? Even one line. I don't need to know anything else. I just haven't heard from him since the weekend, and I'm being silly, probably. Ana

units.author: sam
units.text: ok I lied, one more, Mum rang to say a lost cat in Port Ammet came home after being shut in a shed for days, apparently it was all over the Sound Board, and she wanted me to tell you in case you'd been worried. you didn't know about the cat. nobody did except the whole internet. good night. S x

units.title: Landing stage: planning condition
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi,
A reminder from the planning conditions, since the forums have been quoting them at us: the landing stage has to be left in place, and there's to be no felling within 10 metres of the high water line. The boat crews also like a clear run up from the stage. If anything has come down near it, let me know and I'll note it for the council.
Thanks, Ruth

units.author: sam
units.text: Pip wants to know if there are puffins on your island. I said probably not in winter. she said 'ask anyway'. she also wants to know if you've seen a seal, an otter or 'a whale, even a small one'. I've told her you're very busy with trees, but if you see anything with fins, she would like a full report. S x

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi,
Following up on the trouser recall: replacement pairs in all the usual sizes are now at the Port Ammet office and can go out with the next supply run once the weather clears. If any of the crew are in an affected pair, please keep them off the saw until the new ones arrive, and give them other work.
Thanks, Ruth
